source: FAO-EUFF Food Facility Project (GCP//CMB/033/EC), co-sponsored by the European Union, the Royal Government of Cambodia's Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), and FAO. Presentation: "Techniques for Rice Cultivation and Fertilizer Use" (បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះដំណាំស្រូវ និងការប្រើប្រាស់ជី). Prepared by: Siem Reap Provincial Department of Agriculture (រៀបចំដោយ៖ មន្ត្រីកសិកម្មខេត្តសៀមរាប). Dated June 2010 (មិថុនា ឆ្នាំ២០១០).
text:
This Siem Reap provincial extension guide (FAO-EUFF Food Facility Project, June 2010) gives short, specific guidance on pre-harvest field drainage, harvest timing, grain drying, and on-farm storage equipment.

Field drainage before harvest: Drain all standing water out of the field completely, 7 days before the planned harvest date, so the field and grain can dry down ahead of cutting.

Harvest timing: Harvest the rice when about 85-90% of the grains on the panicle have ripened (turned to mature color), rather than waiting for 100% ripeness, to reduce shattering and field losses.

Grain drying after harvest: Sun-dry the harvested paddy down to a moisture content of about 12-13% before storage, to prevent mold and insect damage during storage.

On-farm storage equipment shown/described: (1) A raised, stilted storage house/barn with corrugated metal siding and a small door -- built off the ground to protect stored paddy from moisture and pests. (2) A woven bamboo/rattan storage basket (built up on a raised wooden platform) for bulk paddy storage. (3) Sealed containers -- a large blue plastic barrel/tank and a metal drum -- used as insect- and moisture-proof storage for smaller quantities of dried paddy.

Data note: the harvest-ripeness threshold (85-90%) and the target drying moisture (12-13%) are broadly consistent with standard Cambodian rice extension guidance seen elsewhere; no discrepancy flagged for these two figures. The 7-day pre-harvest field-drainage window is a specific, useful number not always stated explicitly in other sources.
